summary:
[TO ANGUS TAYLOR1 

Thank you so much for your letter ... this is just a short note to tell you that, and also to express my delight that “Can God Fly? ...” will be coming out. I’ll write as you directed for a copy, and when I do I’ll tell them how much I trea­ sure the article (unless for some incredible reason I forget). My letter that I men­ tioned is in S.F. Commentary, along with the speech, so you will see it, evidently. The last section of your letter really pierced into me keenly, about the umbrella simile and your sense of it. Bruce Gillespie has expressed similar senti­ ments to yours about the amazing power to tie together people that certain writ­ ing has. He makes this so clearly articulate in his comments accompanying my Vancouver speech in S.F. Commentary; things he has written have gotten to me and things I’ve written have gotten to him, until at last, in that issue, we seem to have declared something in concert, some statement of intense emotion. You will, I am sure, see it in that issue—that is, see it with intuition, what both he and I share. Oddly, in 1972, he fell in love with a girl he encountered only briefly; she flew to Australia for a s-f convention and then left forever. It shattered him and his life (if you saw S.F. Commentary #30 you read about it as I did). I say “oddly” because in 1972 that happened to me, at the s-f convention in Vancou­ ver where I delivered that speech.
